  "text": "The curtains were still hanging when Ruth arrived, although her brother had said the flat was empty.

“I couldn’t reach the hooks,” he said.

“You could have brought the steps.”

“They’re here somewhere.”

He opened a cupboard containing a dustpan and a single Wellington boot.

Ruth put her bag on the windowsill. Below, a man was trying to reverse a van between two concrete planters. She watched him get out to inspect the gap.

“Hold the chair,” she said.

Her brother brought it over. Their aunt had covered the seat with green vinyl, folded at the corners and fixed underneath with upholstery tacks. One corner had come loose.

Ruth climbed up and began unfastening the curtain.

“Are you keeping them?” he asked.

“They won’t fit.”

“You could shorten them.”

“My windows are wider.”

He nodded, looking at the chair legs.

At the last hook, the curtain dropped heavily against her shoulder. Dust caught in her throat.

“Careful,” he said, tightening his grip.

She handed it down and stepped onto the floor.

The uncovered window showed a pale rectangle on the opposite wall where the bookcase had stood.

“I found your school photograph,” he said.

“Which one?”

“The one with the fringe.”

“That doesn’t narrow it down.”

He smiled and took an envelope from his jacket. Their aunt had written both their names on the back, though only Ruth was in the picture.

She slid it into her bag.

They folded the curtains together, each holding two corners.

“Charity shop?” he asked.

Ruth ran her thumb over a place where the lining had been mended.

“Let’s shake them out first.”"
